title: Terraform: providers, resources, variables and outputs

videos.script: Lesson one ended on a single file. It described one VPC, and a second apply changed nothing. This lesson takes that file apart, and builds the shop's network out of it. {{files}} A configuration is a directory of files ending in dot tf. One block names the providers it needs. Another sets the region. Each resource block describes one thing that should exist. {{init}} Before anything else, init installs the providers, and writes a lock file. You will see why that file goes into git, and the folder beside it does not. {{plan}} Then the plan. Every line with a plus is something Terraform will create, and nothing happens until you type yes. {{inputs}} Fixed values become variables, so one set of files can describe dev and prod. Outputs go the other way. They hand ids back to people and to scripts. {{providers}} AWS is one provider among many. A random suffix for a bucket and a file on the laptop come from two others. {{destroy}} And at the end, destroy removes all of it. You will look at what it leaves behind, because something does stay.
